searchText: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-2537-bls12-precompile-discussion-thread/4187/76 Would be interesting to see how other libraries fare, I imagine not every client uses constantine None at the moment but Besu and Nimbus are integrating it. EIP-2537 aren't too bad. max 15% perf difference between state-of-the art and slowest on non-MSM operations up to 70% perf difference between Constantine/Gnark and blst for MSM due to BLST not using batch affine additions. BN254 impls are really bad, AFAIK current Nimbus and Besu, and probably Nethermind are using a port of https://github.com/zcash-hackworks/bn/ to their language and this is at minimum 10x slower than kilic's or gnark go implementations. yes We use the fork as well, it's extremely slow, there's one library that's 2x faster, but ultimately it's hard to find bn bindings in rust that are fast _and_ not a nightmare build system wise When you say up to 70% perf different between constantine / gnark and blst, you mean that blst is slower right? yes if you have Nim and Rust installed ``` git clone https://github.com/mratsim/constantine cd constantine cargo test ``` see CI: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L325-L338 and you just pass the input as byte buffer: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/blob/master/constantine-rust/constantine-ethereum-evm-precompiles/src/lib.rs#L62-L111 Given the speed I may write a bench to see what it would take to integrate in revm another venue I was considering is to have an assembly code generator so that Cosntantine directly generates assembly file that can be used with nbindgen, and no nim is needed anymore. can you get portable binaries that way? that would be my only concern I would generate binaries for x86, arm, risc-v, mips, nvidia, amd with a fallback to Nim. with the various relevant OS as well Ihave some of my experiemnts there for AMD, Nvidia GPU: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/tree/master/constantine/math_compiler And reported perf issues to LLVM folks for x86 and ARM: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/pull/456 ``` git clone https://github.com/mratsim/constantine cd constantine CC=clang nimble bench_eth_evm_precompiles ``` You need Nim 1.6.x or Nim 2.0.2, 2.0.4 or latest 2.08 installed. None at the moment but Besu and Nimbus are integrating it.

EIP-2537 aren't too bad.
max 15% perf difference between state-of-the art and slowest on non-MSM operations
up to 70% perf difference between Constantine/Gnark and blst for MSM due to BLST not using batch affine additions.

BN254 impls are really bad, AFAIK current Nimbus and Besu, and probably Nethermind are using a port of https://github.com/zcash-hackworks/bn/ to their language and this is at minimum 10x slower than kilic's or gnark go implementations.
